args.description: Produce a precise report of how qdp.py parses lines, so I can decide where to add case-insensitivity.
args.output_contract: Report: (1) list every line-type branch in the parser with its exact matching condition (quote the code lines, with line numbers); (2) quote verbatim the function(s) that do the dispatch/matching (with line numbers); (3) note any other places in the file that compare command text case-sensitively (e.g., in tests-relevant code or helpers); (4) total line count of file. Quote code exactly as written; do not paraphrase matching conditions.

assert src.count(old1) == 1 and src.count(old2) == 1, (src.count(old1), src.count(old2))
src = src.replace(old1, new1).replace(old2, new2)

assert src.count(old_import) == 1
src = src.replace(old_import, new_import)

anchor = "def test_get_lines_from_qdp(tmp_path):"
assert src.count(anchor) == 1

new_test = '''def test_lowercase_commands(tmp_path):
    # QDP is case insensitive; lowercase (or mixed case) commands must work
    assert _line_type("read serr 1 2") == "command"
    assert _line_type("Read Terr 1") == "command"
    test_file = tmp_path / "test.qdp"
    with open(test_file, "w") as fp:
        print("read serr 1 2", file=fp)
        print("1 0.5 no 0.5", file=fp)

    assert np.all(t["col1_err"] == [0.5, 0.5])
    assert t["col2"].mask[0]
    assert np.all(t["col2_err"] == [0.5, 0.5])

src = src.replace(anchor, new_test + anchor)
open(path, 'w').write(src)
print('test added')

args.summary: Fixed the case-sensitivity bug in astropy.io.ascii.qdp. The line-type classifier in _line_type compiled its QDP command/data regex case-sensitively, so lowercase commands like `read serr 1 2` raised ValueError: Unrecognized QDP line. Two changes in astropy/io/ascii/qdp.py: (1) compiled the line-type regex with re.IGNORECASE so QDP commands (READ SERR/READ TERR, NO data tokens, NAN) are matched case-insensitively, consistent with the QDP spec; (2) changed the per-value `v == "NO"` check in _get_tables_from_qdp_file to `v.upper() == "NO"` so lowercase `no` in data rows is treated as masked. The existing `err_specs[command[1].lower()]` already handled command-word case. Added regression test test_lowercase_commands to astropy/io/ascii/tests/test_qdp.py covering the task's exact reproduction (lowercase `read serr 1 2` file reads into a Table with error columns col1/col1_err/col2/col2_err, plus a lowercase `no` value becoming masked) and a direct _line_type unit check for lowercase and mixed-case commands. Verified: the original repro now succeeds, all 9 tests in test_qdp.py pass, the qdp.py doctests pass, and the full astropy/io/ascii suite (826 passed, 36 skipped, 6 xfailed) passes.

t = Table.read('/tmp/repro.qdp', format='ascii.qdp')
assert t.colnames == ['col1', 'col1_err', 'col2', 'col2_err'], t.colnames
assert list(t['col1']) == [1, 1]
assert list(t['col1_err']) == [0.5, 0.5]
print('repro OK')
"

print(t)
print('col1:', repr(list(t['col1'])))
print('col1_err:', repr(list(t['col1_err'])))
print('dtype:', t['col1'].dtype)
"

cd /testbed && python - <<'EOF'
path = 'astropy/io/ascii/tests/test_qdp.py'
src = open(path).read()
old = '''    assert t.colnames == ["col1", "col1_err", "col2", "col2_err"]
    assert np.all(t["col1"] == [1, 1])

    assert t["col1"] == [1]
    assert t["col1_err"] == [0.5]
    assert t["col2"].mask[0]
    assert t["col2_err"] == [0.5]'''
